title: Design Add and Search Words Data Structure
hints: insert works exactly like a normal trie insert - no wildcards involved there
for search, a plain letter follows one child pointer, just like a regular trie search
the wildcard is where it gets interesting: when you hit a '.', you don't know which child to follow, so try ALL of the current node's children

write search as a recursive function taking (node, position in pattern): if the character at that position is a letter, recurse into that one child if it exists; if it's '.', recurse into every child and return true if ANY of them eventually succeed
the base case: you've consumed the whole pattern, so return whether the current node is marked end-of-word
commonMistakes: treating '.' as matching zero-or-more characters (regex-style) instead of exactly one character
not stopping early once one branch of a wildcard search succeeds, wasting time exploring the rest unnecessarily (a minor efficiency bug, not a correctness one)
forgetting the end-of-word check at the end of the recursion, so a search matches on a prefix that was never actually inserted as a full word

content.problemStatement:
You're given a single space-delimited sequence of operations to run
against an initially empty word dictionary. Each token has one of two
forms:

- "insert:word" - add word to the dictionary, no return value
- "search:pattern" - return 1 if pattern matches any inserted word of the
  SAME length, where each character of pattern is either a lowercase
  letter (must match exactly) or a '.' (matches any single character);
  otherwise return 0

**Simulate the tokens in order, and return a list containing the result of every "search" operation, in the order they occurred.**
constraints: words consist of lowercase English letters only
patterns consist of lowercase English letters and the '.' wildcard
at most 10^4 insert and search operations combined
notes: a pattern that is all wildcards, e.g. '...'
a pattern whose length matches no inserted word's length at all

sampleTestCases.input: ops = "insert:bad insert:dad insert:mad search:pad search:bad search:.ad search:b.."
sampleTestCases.explanation: "pad" was never inserted (0); "bad" matches exactly (1); ".ad" matches "bad" or "dad" (1); "b.." matches "bad" (1)
"a" matches exactly (1); "." matches the single-character word "a" (1); "aa" has no length-2 match (0)
"d.g" and "do." both match "dog" letter-by-letter with one wildcard; "dog." has length 4 but "dog" has length 3, so no match

optimal.time: O(m) per search in the average case, up to O(26^m) worst case with many wildcards
optimal.space: O(total inserted characters) for the trie, O(m) recursion depth per search
optimal.pattern: insert words into a trie; search with backtracking DFS, branching over every child when a '.' is encountered instead of following a single path

bruteForce.approach: keep a plain list of inserted words; for each search, check every word of matching length against the pattern position by position
bruteForce.time: O(n * m) per search, where n is inserted word count and m is pattern length
